jobs.title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Post-Training — Collective Alignment (User Signals)
jobs.description:
Post-training - San Francisco

**About the Team**

The Collective Alignment (User Signals) team is a post-training research team working at the intersection of data science, human feedback, and reinforcement learning. We develop methods for learning from real-world user interactions to build AI systems that deliver lasting value, helping people learn, grow, and accomplish increasingly complex goals with ChatGPT.

Learning from user feedback presents fundamental research challenges: signals are often noisy, biased, and difficult to interpret, and improvements in offline metrics do not always translate into better experiences for users. Our team develops scientific approaches to understanding these signals and translating them into improvements in model behavior through evaluations, reward modeling, and post-training.

**About the Role**

As a Research Engineer or Research Scientist, you will investigate how AI systems can learn from human feedback and real-world usage to better serve users over time.

You will develop new approaches to extracting meaningful learning signals from complex user interactions and incorporating those signals into model training.

This role requires strong deep learning research skills, scientific rigor, and curiosity about how people interact with AI. You will design controlled experiments and ablations, critically examine the relationship between offline evaluations and online model behavior, and work closely with research, product, and data science teams to understand whether improvements translate into meaningful value for users.

**In this role, you will:**

* Develop novel methods for learning from human feedback and user interaction signals.
* Research approaches to incorporating feedback into reward modeling, reinforcement learning, and post-training.
* Design rigorous experiments and ablation studies to isolate the effects of new data, objectives, and training methods.
* Develop offline evaluations and investigate their relationship with online experiments and real-world user outcomes.
* Analyze unexpected results, investigate discrepancies between evaluation metrics and user behavior, and develop hypotheses to guide further research.
* Evaluate tradeoffs and regressions to improve targeted model behaviors while preserving broader capabilities.
* Collaborate with research, alignment, product, and data science teams.
* Implement and debug experiments across large-scale deep learning research systems.

**You might thrive in this role if you:**

* Have a strong background in deep learning research through academic or industry experience.
* Have demonstrated research ability through publications or substantive research contributions in deep learning or LLM post-training.
* Have experience developing new machine learning methods and evaluating them through rigorous, hypothesis-driven experimentation.
* Think critically about experimental design, measurement, and what evaluation results do and do not establish about model behavior.
* Are comfortable designing ablations, investigating surprising results, and reasoning about the relationship between offline metrics and real-world outcomes.
* Have strong programming skills and experience working with complex ML codebases.
* Are curious about how people interact with AI and how those interactions can inform better models.

**Nice to have:**

* Experience with RLHF, reinforcement learning, or modern LLM post-training.
* Research or demonstrated interest in AI alignment, human feedback, or user signals.
* Experience with online experimentation, evaluation methodology, or learning from noisy and biased feedback.
* Experience connecting machine learning research with real-world product behavior.

**Member of Technical Staff - Machine Learning Research Engineer I**  
  
San Francisco Bay Area | Bellevue, Washington
  
  
**About AIVista**  
  
NTT DATA AIVista, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of NTT DATA, is based in Silicon Valley. We develop AI products for enterprises operating in complex regulatory environments. We work with NTT DATA Inc., NTT DATA Japan, and NTT DOCOMO to deploy systems for NTT clients. Our clients combine AIVista's product AI expertise with NTT DATA's industry knowledge and systems-integration experience.  
  
**The Role**  
  
The Machine Learning Research Engineer works closely with AIVista scientists to turn promising research into dependable capabilities for enterprise use. You will develop a deep understanding of each method, its assumptions, supporting evidence, and known limitations, then focus on the work required to make it reproducible, robust, scalable, and maintainable.  
  
You will test how methods behave across realistic workloads, varied domains and data, difficult edge cases, and operational constraints; improve their reliability and efficiency; and integrate them into product capabilities with the traceability, controls, and review boundaries required in regulated industries. This work spans reinforcement learning, simulation environments, formal methods, autoformalization, and AIVista's data, rule, action, and process ontologies.  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Work with scientists to understand each method's assumptions, supporting evidence, known failure modes, and acceptance criteria for broader use.
* Reproduce research results across independent runs and settings, characterize sources of variance, and identify behavior that depends on a narrow dataset, model version, configuration, or operating condition.
* Refactor and extend research prototypes without changing their scientific meaning; make tradeoffs explicit and validate each material change against agreed baselines.
* Design stress tests, adversarial cases, counterfactual scenarios, rare events, and out-of-distribution evaluations that expose brittle behavior before product use.
* Scale methods from research-sized examples to realistic workflow length, data volume, concurrency, and domain variation while controlling latency and cost.
* Improve reliability, calibration, constraint adherence, recovery behavior, and consistency, and determine whether measured gains generalize beyond the original research cases.
* Advance synthetic environments, workflow simulations, and agent evaluations from research prototypes into stable, versioned assets that represent exceptions, human review, governed actions, and external-system behavior.
* Harden autoformalization and ontology-backed methods so source traceability, rule and process semantics, validation evidence, and governed actions remain correct as content and scale change.
* Preserve independent checks and acceptance evidence as models, code, data, ontologies, and process definitions evolve.
* Feed findings back to Science, including failures that require changes to the problem formulation, learning method, reward or constraint design, formalization approach, or evaluation strategy.
* Partner with product and engineering teams to define operating limits, monitoring, regression tests, release criteria, rollback plans, and ownership for capabilities moving into production.
* Build the durable software and automation required for reproducible experimentation, repeated evaluation, efficient scaling, and safe product integration, and maintain clear documentation for future contributors.

**Qualifications**  
  
**Basic**

* Master's degree in computer science, machine learning, artificial intelligence, software engineering, applied mathematics, or a related field.
* At least 5 years of experience taking machine-learning or research prototypes toward reliable, sustained use at realistic scale.

* Demonstrated experience improving the reproducibility, robustness, scalability, or operating efficiency of a research capability, supported by clear measurements and failure analysis.
* Strong software-engineering judgment, including the ability to restructure prototypes, isolate assumptions, design effective tests, diagnose performance and reliability problems, and leave maintainable code and documentation.
* Working knowledge of machine learning, statistical evaluation, experimental design, and failure analysis, with the ability to implement methods from papers and reason about how engineering changes affect the method.
* Experience evaluating behavior across changing data, model versions, workloads, and operating conditions rather than relying on a single benchmark result.
* Ability to collaborate closely with scientists, engineers, product teams, and domain experts to move research capabilities toward reliable use in regulated environments.

**Preferred**

* Experience hardening reinforcement-learning environments, agent systems, workflow simulations, digital twins, or other sequential-decision methods for use beyond research demonstrations.
* Experience evaluating long-horizon agents, verifier-guided methods, or reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards under adversarial, rare, or changing conditions.
* Experience scaling ontology-backed, knowledge-graph, rule, process, or provenance-aware methods while preserving semantic correctness and source traceability.

* Experience diagnosing distribution shift, specification gaming, reward hacking, data leakage, calibration failures, or regressions that appear only at larger scale.

jobs.description:
**Member of Technical Staff - Applied Scientist I**  
**Formal Methods for AI Driven Software Development Life Cycle**  
  
San Francisco Bay Area | Bellevue, Washington | Hybrid |  
  
**About AIVista**  
  
NTT DATA AIVista, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of NTT DATA, is based in Silicon Valley. We develop AI products for enterprises operating in complex regulatory environments. We work with NTT DATA Inc., NTT DATA Japan, and NTT DOCOMO to deploy systems for NTT clients. Our clients combine AIVista's product AI expertise with NTT DATA's industry knowledge and systems-integration experience.  
  
**The Role**  
  
The Applied Scientist will develop methods that turn natural-language intent into structured, machine-checkable artifacts and use those artifacts to make AI-driven software development more verifiable, traceable, and reliable. You will work from policies, regulations, standard operating procedures, requirements, process descriptions, application programming interfaces, and code to construct formal specifications, rule ontologies, process ontologies, contracts, tests, and proofs with complete source traceability.  
  
The work addresses two distinct assurance problems. Validation asks whether a formal artifact faithfully captures authorized intent. Verification asks whether an implementation satisfies that artifact. You will build measurable validation methods for omissions and mistranslations, integrate independent checkers and proof systems, and carry the resulting evidence through the AI-driven software development life cycle. The objective is a practical development workflow in which models may propose requirements, designs, code, tests, or proofs, while deterministic checkers, versioned evidence, and human authority determine what is accepted.  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Develop autoformalization methods that translate policies, procedures, regulations, requirements, and process descriptions into typed rules, process models, contracts, and formal specifications.
* Design restricted domain-specific languages and formal semantics that domain experts and engineers can review together, with clause-level provenance and versioned change histories.
* Build validation stacks using controlled source language, concretization, counterexamples, back-translation, cross-representation consistency, independent dual translation, and expert adjudication.
* Create specification-mutation, non-vacuity, and seeded-defect benchmarks that measure detection rates for omissions, weakenings, exception errors, and mistranslations.
* Integrate satisfiability modulo theories solvers, model checkers, theorem provers, static analyzers, type systems, and property-based or fuzz testing into independent verification harnesses.
* Develop verifier-guided generation and repair methods for specifications, code, tests, invariants, proofs, and counterexamples while keeping the checker outside the generative model's trusted path.
* Apply formal methods across the AI-driven software development life cycle, from requirements and architecture through model-generated implementation, continuous integration, release evidence, monitoring, and change-impact analysis.
* Study composition at system scale, proof and specification maintenance under change, and methods for preserving evidence across tool, model, dependency, and compiler versions.
* Connect formal artifacts to AIVista's data, rule, action, and process ontologies so runtime decisions can be traced to governing sources, versions, evaluated values, and accepted checks.
* Define assurance claims with explicit scope, assumptions, trusted components, checker versions, and acceptance boundaries; prevent stronger claims than the evidence supports.
* Partner with product and engineering teams to transition successful methods into production authoring, verification, and AI-driven software development workflows.
* Lead publications, patents, open-source contributions, and research partnerships in formal methods, programming languages, software engineering, knowledge representation, and AI-driven software development.

NTT DATA AIVista | Formal Methods for AI Driven Software Development Life CyclePage
  
  
**Qualifications**  
  
**Basic**

* PhD in computer science, programming languages, formal methods, software engineering, artificial intelligence, mathematics, or a related field, or equivalent industry impact.
* At least 5 years of experience in formal methods, software engineering research, artificial intelligence, or machine learning, with significant experience applying research in production environments.
* A proven record of impactful research demonstrated through publications, patents, open-source tools, formal artifacts, or shipped software products.
* Deep experience in at least two relevant areas: formal specification, program verification, model checking, theorem proving, static analysis, type systems, program synthesis, requirements engineering, or autoformalization.
* Hands-on experience building with at least one proof assistant, theorem prover, satisfiability solver, model checker, static analyzer, or verification-aware language.
* Strong foundations in logic, algorithms, semantics, software architecture, and experimental design, with the ability to state exactly what a check proves and assumes.
* Proficiency in Python and at least one additional production language, with experience building research prototypes and developer tools that engineering teams can maintain.

**Preferred**

* Experience with large-language-model autoformalization, neural theorem proving, verifier-guided generation, proof repair, or AI-driven program synthesis and code generation.
* Experience with controlled natural language, specification mining, domain-specific languages, traceability, or translating requirements into executable artifacts.
* Experience with ontologies, semantic modeling languages, description logics, graph constraint languages, rule engines, or policy-as-co

**Member of Technical Staff - Applied Scientist I**  
**Reinforcement Learning and Simulation Environments**  
  
San Francisco Bay Area | Bellevue, Washington | Hybrid |  
  
**About AIVista**  
  
NTT DATA AIVista, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of NTT DATA, is based in Silicon Valley. We develop AI products for enterprises operating in complex regulatory environments. We work with NTT DATA Inc., NTT DATA Japan, and NTT DOCOMO to deploy systems for NTT clients. Our clients combine AIVista's product AI expertise with NTT DATA's industry knowledge and systems-integration experience.  
  
**The Role**  
  
The Applied Scientist will build the learning environments that let AIVista train and evaluate agents before they act in real regulated workflows. You will convert business processes, rules, governed actions, systems of record, documents, and event logs into synthetic, versioned simulations with explicit state, observations, actions, constraints, human-review points, and terminal outcomes.  
  
This role blends reinforcement learning research with environment engineering. You will design reward and cost functions, generate curricula and counterfactual cases, validate simulator fidelity against real operations, and develop offline, safe, constrained, and multi-agent learning methods. The objective is not a demonstration that optimizes a proxy. It is a training and evaluation system that exposes reward hacking, respects governed action boundaries, and predicts whether a policy improves process outcomes without creating unacceptable risk.  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Build synthetic environments and workflow digital twins for regulated enterprise processes, including stochastic events, exceptions, human decisions, delays, and external-system behavior.
* Translate process models, rule sets, action contracts, event logs, and operational policies into Markov decision processes, partially observable models, stochastic games, and discrete-event simulations.
* Define state, observation, action, termination, reward, cost, and constraint interfaces that are faithful to the underlying workflow and reusable across training and evaluation.
* Design reward functions and verifiers, then test them for specification gaming, shortcut learning, reward tampering, and unintended incentives using adversarial and hidden evaluation cases.
* Validate environment fidelity against production traces, process-mining results, subject-matter expert review, and counterfactual scenarios; quantify where the simulation does not represent the real process.
* Generate synthetic trajectories, rare-event scenarios, and curriculum stages that improve coverage while preserving provenance and reproducibility.
* Develop algorithms across offline, safe, constrained, model-based, hierarchical, and multi-agent reinforcement learning, as well as imitation and preference-based learning where appropriate.
* Integrate deterministic rule checks, governed actions, safety constraints, and human-review policies into training and rollout evaluation.
* Create benchmarks for sample efficiency, generalization, constraint violations, robustness, calibration, latency, cost, and process-level outcomes.
* Build scalable environment runners, trajectory stores, experiment infrastructure, and reproducible evaluation pipelines with engineering partners.
* Move successful research into production decision-support and agent-training systems, with monitoring for distribution shift and policy regressions.
* Lead publications, patents, open-source contributions, and external research partnerships when they advance AIVista's product and science objectives.

**Qualifications**  
  
**Basic**

* PhD in computer science, machine learning, artificial intelligence, operations research, industrial engineering, applied mathematics, or a related field, or equivalent industry impact.

* At least 5 years of experience in artificial intelligence or machine learning, with significant experience applying science and research in production environments.
* A proven record of impactful research demonstrated through publications, patents, open-source systems, benchmarks, or shipped AI products.
* Deep experience designing reinforcement-learning environments, simulators, reward functions, or sequential-decision systems, not only training policies in existing benchmarks.
* Strong foundations in reinforcement learning, stochastic processes, optimization, statistical methods, causal reasoning, and experimental design.
* Proficiency in Python and a modern machine-learning framework, with experience building reliable research software that engineering teams can transition to production.
* Ability to work with domain experts and translate operational processes, controls, and failure modes into precise learning and evaluation artifacts.

**Preferred**

* Experience with offline, safe or constrained, multi-agent, model-based, hierarchical, or risk-sensitive reinforcement learning.
* Experience designing and implementing custom single-agent or multi-agent learning environments, scalable environment runners, and discrete-event process simulations.
* Experience with process mining, Business Process Model and Notation, workflow engines, digital twins, operations research, scheduling, or queueing systems.
* Experience with language-model agents, reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, verifier-guided training, tool-use agents, or long-horizon agent benchmarks.
* Experience detecting reward hacking, specification gaming, data leakage, simulator exploitation, or overfitting to public evaluation cases.
* Experience with synthetic data, counterfactual generation, domain randomization, curriculum design, rare-event simulation, or sim-to-real evaluation.
* Experience using ontologies, rule systems, action schemas, event logs, or system-of-record interfaces to define environment semantics.
* Experience deploying

### **About the Role**

Join a software engineering team building AI systems for hospitality operations. You will own full-stack components that help resolve guest requests, from understanding intent and retrieving relevant information to coordinating tools and generating responses.

* Develop retrieval systems that ground responses in accurate, current customer data.
* Create reliable orchestration for multi-step workflows, including recovery from third-party API failures.

* Implement observability and tracing to make complex agent workflows understandable to support teams.
* Develop interfaces and controls that let support leads configure agent behavior without code.

* Experience designing and debugging production AI or machine learning systems, including retrieval, prompt engineering, or model orchestration.
* Experience evaluating retrieval systems and building multi-step workflows, tool orchestration, or function-calling systems.

$130,000 to $220,000 base salary annually, plus 0.20% to 1.20% equity. Health insurance and a 401(k) match are provided. Visa sponsorship is not available.

On-site in San Francisco, California.

**Overview**
------------

This is a role on the Business Disruption Team at Intuit. We are a high-octane, entrepreneurial group on a mission to build net-new disruptive products and supercharge our existing ecosystem with AI-first technologies. We operate like a nimble startup within the broader Intuit organization.

You will be working alongside an elite, dynamic mix of seasoned Intuit veterans and brilliant newcomers to the company. This is a team composed of proven leaders with deep track records of success across the organization. By combining deep institutional knowledge with fresh, disruptive perspectives, we create an environment where you will be challenged, mentored, and inspired to do the best work of your career.

We are looking for an exceptional Full-Stack Software Engineer who thrives in ambiguity, operates with a high degree of autonomy, and moves with blistering speed. In this role, you won't just be writing code, you will be leveraging the latest AI coding tools to dramatically accelerate your output, running rapid experiments directly with customers, and bringing zero-to-one concepts to life. If you are a builder who loves to ship fast, learn continuously, and have a lot of fun doing it, you belong here.

**Responsibilities**

* Rapid Development & Execution: Design, build, and ship full-stack software solutions with an intense focus on velocity and getting things done.
* AI-Accelerated Engineering: Extensively leverage AI coding assistants and modern tooling to write, test, and deploy code faster and more efficiently than traditional methods.
* Customer-Centric Experimentation: Work on the front lines with end-users to conduct rapid product experiments, gather real-world feedback, and iterate quickly based on data.
* Autonomous Navigation: Operate comfortably in a fast-paced environment with a high degree of ambiguity, taking extreme ownership of your projects from inception to launch.
* Disruptive Innovation: Build entirely new, AI-native products from scratch while also identifying ways to accelerate existing Intuit products with cutting-edge tech.

**Qualifications**

* Technical & Craft Expertise: Proven experience as a Full-Stack Software Engineer building modern, scalable applications across both the frontend and backend. Typescript + Python is what we use.
* AI Tooling Fluency: Hands-on experience and deep comfort using AI coding tools. Have the ability to clearly express your intent and exercise good judgement to direct AI to produce clear and maintainable code (not AI slop).
* Startup Mentality: An aggressively entrepreneurial spirit with a track record of moving fast, cutting through red tape, and delivering results quickly.
* Customer Obsession: A strong desire to be close to the customer, with demonstrated experience running A/B tests, prototypes, or rapid user experiments.
* Adaptability & Autonomy: The ability to self-direct, pivot rapidly when hypotheses are disproven, and thrive in an unstructured, highly ambiguous environment.
* Growth Mindset: A relentless appetite for learning new technologies, taking calculated risks, and having a blast while building the future.

Intuit provides a competitive compensation package with a strong pay for performance rewards approach. This position may be eligible for a cash bonus, equity rewards and benefits, in accordance with our applicable plans and programs (see more about our compensation and benefits at Intuit®: Careers | Benefits). Pay offered is based on factors such as job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and work location. To drive ongoing fair pay for employees, Intuit conducts regular comparisons across categories of ethnicity and gender.

The expected base pay range for this position is:
  
Mountain View $140,500 - $190,000
